description.narrative: Building Resilient Refugees and Host Communities. Uganda continues to host the largest refugee population in Africa with over 1,423 million refugees displaced by conflicts in the neighboring countries.

condition.narrative: Consistent with the Article III of the SBAA [or the Supplemental Provisions to the Project Document], the responsibility for the safety and security of the Implementing Partner and its personnel and property, and of UNDP’s property in the Implementing Partner’s custody, rests with the Implementing Partner. To this end, the Implementing Partner shall: a) put in place an appropriate security plan and maintain the security plan, taking into account the security situation in the country where the project is being carried; b) assume all risks and liabilities related to the Implementing Partner’s security, and the full implementation of the security plan.

Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

description.narrative:
Output 1: Sustainable and green livelihood opportunities expanded for refugees and host communities in West Nile (Adjumani and Obongi districts) for environmental conservation Output Indicator: 1.1.# of refugees and host communities’ individuals (60% women) engaged in environmentally friendly livelihood activities. Output Indicator 1.2. # of refugees and host communities’ households trained in environmental management practices.
Output 2: Capacities of targeted District Local Governments are strengthened to implement the CRRF sector plans, COVID-19 response and recovery plans. Indicator 2.1: # of District Local Governments who receive capacity building to effective respond to and mitigate the spread of COVID-19 Indicator 2.2: # of Districts with capacities built to respond to COVID 19 Indicator 2.3: # of Key District Local Government staff with capacities (inclusive of refugee welfare committees) strengthened to respond to shocks and pandemics.
Output 3: Peaceful co-existence among refugee and host communities enhanced. Indicator: 3.1. Number of peace education campaigns conducted to promote social cohesion, including facilitating inter-cultural dialogue for peace among refugees and host communities. Indicator 3.2. Number of inter-cultural dialogues conducted.

Results attained under output 1 Result for indicator target 1.1: 1,370 out of 1320 refugees and host communities’ individuals (60% women) have engaged in environmentally friendly livelihood activities. Result for indicator target 1.2: 1,320 refugees and host communities’ households are trained in environmental management practices.
Output 2: Capacities of targeted District Local Governments are strengthened to implement the CRRF sector plans, COVID-19 response and recovery plans.
Results attained under output 2 Result for indicator target 2.1: Two (2) District Local Governments received capacity building to effectively respond to and mitigate the spread of COVID-19. Result for indicator target 2.2:Two (2) Districts including Obongi and Adjumani had their capacities built to respond to COVID-19. Result for indicator target 2.3: Fourty (40) Key District Local Government staff with capacities (inclusive of refugee welfare committees) strengthened to respond to shocks and pandemics.
Results attained under output 3 Result for indicator target 3.1: 40 out of 20 (200%) peace education campaigns conducted to promote social cohesion, including facilitating inter-cultural dialogue for peace among refugees and host communities.
